paragraphs.text: Render mermaid fenced code blocks as diagrams in DeepSeek Harness.
# dsh-mermaid
Render mermaid fenced code blocks as diagrams in DSH markdown.

A DeepSeek Harness plugin,
packaged as a DSH bundle: `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, and

`cordis.patch.yml` inserts the `mermaid` row into the active profile.
The client half is served fro
m `lib/client.js` (`dsh.client.platform: web`).
## Where it renders

The harness markdown renderer exposes no custom-code-block seam, so the client half
post-processes t

he rendered DOM: it finds fenced code that is a mermaid diagram, renders it
with mermaid and swaps t

he code view for the diagram. Because the sweep observes
`document.body`, every surface that renders
markdown through the shared renderer is covered:

- chat messages and the code cards they contain (including streaming and re-renders);
- the **right

Sidebar document preview** for `.md`/`.markdown` files — the diagram keeps the
card header with its

copy button and gains the plugin's zoom/fit toolbar;
- theme switches re-render every diagram with t

ains the plugin's zoom/fit toolbar;
- theme switches re-render every diagram with the other palette.

Deliberately left as code: the plain-text source view of the preview
(`[data-textpreview-plain]`), d

iff views, and blocks whose source only starts with a diagram
keyword (a list of keywords, prose tha
t mentions `graph TD`).
## Install

- Desktop app: **Plugins** → install `github:bosenok/dsh-mermaid` (private repository:
give the mach

ine git access), then enable the bundle.
- CLI: `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:bosenok/d

sh-mermaid`.
- Local checkout: `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add file:/path/to/dsh-mermaid`.

Enabling the bundle mounts the plugin; HMR applies it to a running app, and a
restart makes sure the
client half is rebuilt.

> Note for the app-managed `desktop` profile: `dsh plugin --profile desktop add`
> only installs the

dependency and copies the package; unlike a regular profile
> it does not enable the bundle. Enable

it by adding the package name to
> `dsh.profile.bundles` in `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json`

(or through the
> Plugins page). Other profiles enable the installed bundle automatically.
